text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1% today to $387, continuing a sharp five-day rally that's added 7% to the stock since late August. The move reflects a spike in crude oil prices driven by escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran's retaliatory strikes on U.S. Gulf allies and reports of mines in the Hormuz Strait have pushed Brent crude above $95 a barrel and U.S. crude to $91.48. For a refiner like Marathon, higher oil prices and tighter global supply conditions are a tailwind: refineries are running at 98% capacity with lean inventory levels (gasoline and diesel stockpiles are both relatively low), meaning the company is running flat-out to meet demand at margins improved by the oil-price spike.

This rally fits into a broader pattern where Middle East disruptions have consistently boosted energy stocks over the past week. The combination of full refinery utilization and constrained product supplies means Marathon can pass through input cost increases while benefiting from the wider spread between crude and finished products—essentially locking in stronger profits as long as tensions keep oil elevated.
